sec: T1DM markers, autoimmunity and antibody interpretation

items.q: Match the following Type 1 autoantibody to its prevalence / target — 1) GAD65 2) IA-2 3) ZnT8 4) Anti-insulin … A) ~70–80% at diagnosis B) ~60–70% at diagnosis C) >95% in some populations D) More common in children
items.exp: GAD65 is positive in roughly 70–80% at diagnosis; IA-2 in 60–70%; ZnT8 in over 95% in some populations; anti-insulin is more common in children. (Book p923)

items.q: A 22-year-old non-obese patient has new diabetes, positive GAD and rapidly progresses to insulin. The most consistent diagnosis is:
items.exp: Non-obese young adult with GAD positivity and rapid progression fits Type 1 diabetes. (Book p923)

items.q: Assess these facts: I HLA-DRB1*04 increases Type 1 risk. IIGAD antibodies are also seen in stiff-person syndrome.
items.exp: HLA-DRB1*04 is a susceptibility allele for Type 1 diabetes; GAD antibodies also occur in stiff-person syndrome and cerebellar ataxia. (Book p923)

items.q: Which is the odd one out — an antibody NOT typically associated with Type 1 diabetes?
items.exp: Anti-CCP is associated with rheumatoid arthritis, not Type 1 diabetes. (Book p923)

items.q: ZnT8 antibodies target the zinc transporter in pancreatic ___ cells.
items.exp: ZnT8 is expressed in pancreatic β-cells, making it a specific autoimmune target. (Book p923)

items.q: Match the following test to its use in T1DM — 1) C-peptide 2) Autoantibody panel 3) HbA1c 4) Insulin level … A) Reflects endogenous insulin secretion B) Classifies autoimmune diabetes C) Monitors chronic glycaemia D) Affected by exogenous insulin and hepatic clearance
items.exp: C-peptide measures endogenous insulin secretion; autoantibody panel classifies autoimmune diabetes; HbA1c monitors chronic glycaemia; insulin level is confounded by exogenous insulin and hepatic clearance. (Book p923)

items.q: An 18-year-old with new T1DM has undetectable C-peptide and positive ZnT8. The most consistent interpretation is:
opts: Autoimmune β-cell destruction with no residual function
Type 2 diabetes with severe insulin resistance
items.exp: Undetectable C-peptide with ZnT8 indicates autoimmune β-cell failure in Type 1 diabetes. (Book p923)

items.q: Assess T1DM genetic risk: I HLA-DR3 and DR4 increase risk. II Most T1DM is monogenic.
items.exp: HLA-DR3 and DR4 (DRB1*03 and *04) increase susceptibility; most T1DM is polygenic, not monogenic. (Book p923)

items.q: Match the following antibody to the population where it's most useful — 1) Insulin autoantibody 2) GAD 2) ZnT8 3) IA-2 … A) Children <5 yr at onset B) Adults >30 yr at onset C) Combined with GAD for sensitivity D) Highly specific for T1DM
items.exp: Insulin autoantibody is most useful in young children; GAD is more often positive in adult-onset T1DM/LADA; ZnT8 combined with GAD improves sensitivity; IA-2 is highly specific for T1DM. (Book p923)

items.q: A 5-year-old with new diabetes has positive insulin autoantibodies but negative GAD and IA-2. The most consistent interpretation is:
items.exp: Insulin autoantibodies are common in young children with T1DM; one antibody plus clinical phenotype is sufficient to support diagnosis. (Book p923)

items.q: Triple antibody positivity (GAD, IA-2, ZnT8) in a newly diagnosed adult is highly suggestive of ___ rather than Type 2.
items.exp: Triple positivity in adults strongly suggests autoimmune diabetes (Type 1-like or LADA). (Book p923)

items.q: Assess C-peptide: I It is cleaved from proinsulin in equimolar amounts. II C-peptide is a surrogate for endogenous insulin.
items.exp: C-peptide is cleaved from proinsulin in equimolar amounts with insulin and is used as a surrogate for endogenous insulin secretion. (Book p923)
